thread:
lina-cs: Heads up — Copperleaf reported a big p99 spike on /v1/embeddings around 02:00 UTC, lots of 504s and long tails. They say it started after a batch job kicked off from their side but we see system-wide IO backpressure in the same window.

mark-eng: can you paste a couple request IDs + sample payload sizes? need to check batching and model choice.

lina-cs: sure — sample req ids: req_0a1b2c, req_0a1b2d. payloads mostly 100–300 texts per call, avg token count ~1200. Model: open-embed-xl (quantized). They said rate didn't change drastically but one of their clients did a bulk import at 01:58 UTC.

sara-sre: looking at infra metrics now — cluster embed-worker-7 shows nvme iowait spike and GPU host queuing that matches 01:58–02:12 window. p95 for that host jumped from 90ms to 1.6s, p99 to ~4.8s. There are a few other tenants with sudden bursty embed patterns (tenant:northbridge), could be noisy neighbor hitting shared cache/IO.

mark-eng: if northbridge is spiking parallel small requests it can cause contention at the host NVMe layer (cache eviction) which cascades into slower KV cache loads and higher latency. We saw similar behavior in Q3 with small-batch embeds causing IO thrashing.

lina-cs: Copperleaf is on a Dedicated reservation but not pinned to a specific host — reservation is pool-level. They want a short-term fix and a more durable mitigation.

devon-plat: immediate options: 1) apply a per-tenant throttle cap for noisy tenants (northbridge) to smooth ingress; 2) create a temporary allowlist rule so Copperleaf requests bypass global backpressure for the next 6 hours; 3) injest request-level caching for repeated items if payloads overlap. Which do we want to do now?

mark-eng: I'd prefer (1) + (2) — throttle the noisy tenant first to stop active thrash, then add allowlist for Copperleaf so they don't get killed by our circuit-breakers while we stabilize. Need SRE to implement throttle rule quickly.

sara-sre: I can push a throttle rule to the rate-limiter. Suggest: northbridge -> max_concurrent_requests: 8, token_rate_limit: 2000/min for next 4 hours. For Copperleaf allowlist, we add an override in backpressure policy: bypass_threshold: true for tenant_id: tenant_copperleaf for 6 hours. Roll back after monitoring.

mark-eng: also add a KV cache warming policy for Copperleaf on the hot hosts if possible (prefetch top prefixes from their recent traffic) — that should reduce IO at first-touch.

lina-cs: Copperleaf asked if we can also increase their reserved qps while we investigate. They offered to pay for a short burst reservation.

devon-plat: we can provision a short-lived reservation slice. We should coordinate with finance for billing. I'll open a support-reservation ticket and link it here.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rate-limiter update pushed to canary in us-west-2 | change-id: rl-20260302-11 | northbridge throttle applied.

mark-eng: can everyone check logs for error surfaces? I'm seeing elevated kv_store misses at the same time — stack excerpt: 
```
2026-03-02T01:59:21Z embed-worker-7 ERROR kv_get failed key=prefix_0x3 status=ETIMEDOUT
2026-03-02T01:59:21Z embed-worker-7 WARN fallback to cold load took=420ms
2026-03-02T01:59:22Z embed-worker-7 INFO request=req_0a1b2c total_latency=3120ms
```

mark-eng: that ETIMEDOUT is the NVMe layer; throttling northbridge should drop parallel cold loads.

sara-sre: throttle deployed. I've also created a short-term allowlist entry for tenant_copperleaf in the backpressure policy; config snippet below: 
```
allowlist:
  tenants:
    - id: "tenant_copperleaf"
      bypass_backpressure: true
      expires_at: "2026-03-02T08:00:00Z"
```

lina-cs: thanks — Copperleaf confirmed 20% reduction in 504s within 10 mins. They're still seeing occasional p99 blips ~1.1s but better than 4–5s.

mark-eng: next steps: 1) schedule KV cache prefetch for Copperleaf on hosts where their traffic lands; 2) add longer-term per-tenant qps reservations for high-value tenants; 3) look into host-level IO isolation (cgroup/blkio tuning) to avoid cross-tenant nvme thrash. I'll open two engineering tickets for (1) and (3).

sara-sre: monitoring alert rules updated to surface nvme_iowait per-host and correlate with per-tenant request rate. Also added a dashboard tile for tenant-level p99 on embeds.

lina-cs: I've told Copperleaf we'll keep the allowlist in place until 08:00 UTC and partner on a short reservation. They're happy for now and want a follow-up post-mortem.

devon-plat: created internal ticket INF-1722 for reservation + billing handoff. Assigning to @mark-eng for kernel/IO investigation and @sara-sre for rollout verification.

mark-eng: I'll also add a small changelog note in release channel once the KV prefetch PR lands.

ops-bot: ticket INF-1722 created | link: https://redwood.atlassian.example/browse/INF-1722

lina-cs: thanks everyone — will keep monitoring and will post the post-mortem once we collect metrics. :thumbsup:
